newsitem.title: BRAZIL: GM Brazil unit signs $600 mln plant deal.
newsitem.headline: GM Brazil unit signs $600 mln plant deal.

text.p: General Motors Corp's Brazilian affiliate said Monday it signed a deal to build a $600 million assembly plant in the southern state of Rio Grande do Sul.

General Motors do Brasil will start building the plant this year in Gravatai, about 30 km from Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul's capital, said a company spokesman after the companby and state officials formalized the agreement.
Operations should start in 1999, he said. The automaker did not disclose the plant's output capacity but said the new facility will create 2,000 direct jobs.
The facility, which will be GM's third plant in Brazil and the first in the country's southern region, will serve the neighboring Mercosur coutries of Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay.
"Part of the production will be sold in the domestic market and part will be exported to Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay," the company spokesman said.
The Gravatai's plant is part of GM's $1.250 billion expansion plan which also includes the construction of two other plants in Brazil.
One will be located in Mogi das Cruzes, about 70 km from Sao Paulo city, and the other will be built in the southern state of Santa Catarina but the site has yet to be determined.
The spokesman also said the $600 million total investment will include funds from suppliers.
Last week, Chrysler Corp signed an agreement to build a $315 million Dakota pick-up truck plant in the southern state of Parana to also strengthen its presence in the Mercosur region.
